name: Ireland

choices.married: Married or civil partners, one income

items.label: Pension contribution
items.note: Your contribution to an occupational pension, PRSA or personal pension.

items.label: Pay for income tax
items.note: Pension contributions get income tax relief within age-related limits, from 15% of earnings under 30 to 40% at 60 and over, on earnings up to €115,000. USC and PRSI are still charged on the full salary.

items.label: Tax credits
items.note: Personal credit €2,125 (€4,250 married) and employee (PAYE) credit €2,125.

items.label: Income tax
items.note: 20% up to €46,500 (€55,500 for a married couple with one income), 40% above, less tax credits.

items.label: Universal Social Charge
items.note: 0.5% to €12,012, 2% to €30,300, 3% to €70,044, 8% above. Nothing is due on incomes of €13,000 or less.

items.label: PRSI
items.note: Class A: 4.35% until September and 4.5% from 1 October 2027, 4.3875% over the year. Nothing below €352 a week, and a tapering PRSI credit up to €424 a week.

items.label: Pension contribution
items.note: Taken from pay before income tax.

assumptions: PAYE employee paying Class A PRSI
No children; married means one spouse earns the whole salary and the couple is jointly assessed
Any pension contribution entered is within your age-related limit for tax relief
notModelled: Pension contributions (tax relief at the marginal rate)
Other tax credits (rent, home carer, single person child carer)
Reduced USC rates for medical card holders and over-70s
provisional: The PRSI credit (up to €12 a week, tapering between €352 and €424 a week) is the 2026 one; Budget 2027 announced no change to it
